chapter: Savoy days, the Concord and business
title: Playing in a quartet
summary: With a rhythm section he kept the same swing beat and big-band tunes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Right. And, a little while back, too, you mentioned that you also worked as a quartet for awhile. You know, was that similar in any way to the type of quartet form, let's say, that Jones Jones used a lot?
Well, I guess it would, in members, that's all. It was like a rhythm section and myself.

But, I had a different style. I had, I was working, playing on the same style and the same music that I was using with my big band. I didn't go into that. I just did my same feeling on the same swing beat that I had. That's what I still do now. You know? You know the songs like "Tippin' In"? I'd do that, but I'll just play the saxophone solo on the trumpet. I do the "A Train". I do all the big things, big band things, you know. And then, I do an arrangement with the clarinet now. I did it with the quartet also. I let the piano player take two choruses instead
of one. Give me a little, stretch it out. You know?
